intro: On a Mac, Gmail for podcast producers means the Gmail website open in Safari or Chrome. A third-party Mac guide says there has never been an official Gmail app for Mac. The work that matters is pitching guests, following up and scheduling sends. Gmail handles all three in the browser, and this page shows where each setting lives.
tldr: Turn on templates first: Settings > See all settings > Advanced, then Templates > Enable.
Templates only work on a computer. Do the setup at your Mac, not in the phone app.
Scheduled send lives on the arrow beside Send. Gmail allows up to 100 scheduled emails. Cancel send turns one back into a draft.
Deleted templates cannot be recovered, so copy good pitches somewhere safe first.
Lazur points at controls, guides you click by click, drafts and dictates. It does not click Send for you.

blocks.text: Gmail app for Mac: what you actually get

You do not install Gmail on a Mac the way you install a normal app. You open the Gmail website in Safari or Chrome and work there. A third-party Mac guide says Gmail in a browser is fine, but it competes with every other tab for memory. If you keep a lot of tabs open during a recording week, you will notice it.

blocks.text: The Chrome shortcut is the option most producers ask about. It gives Gmail its own Dock icon and window, which helps when Gmail is your main tool. The trade-off is alerts. Those are browser notifications, not native macOS app notifications, so plan around that before you rely on them. The same guide also says that with the Chrome shortcut, multiple Google accounts share one sign-in session. One security check can log you out of all of them.

Apple's Safari User Guide page on adding websites to the Dock did not show steps for Gmail when it was checked. The Safari and Chrome steps for pinning Gmail are in [Pin Gmail to the Dock on Mac](/how-to/pin-gmail-to-the-dock-in-gmail).
Set up Gmail templates on a Mac for guest pitches

Templates are the first setting to change. Google now calls them templates. Older guides call the same feature canned responses, so you may see that name in search results. The idea is simple. You write a pitch once, save it, then insert it when you need it.

Reuse has a cost. Guests notice pitches that look copied. One podcaster quoted in a Buzzsprout guest survey put it bluntly: "if it's clearly copy/pasted, too long, or shows zero understanding of my audience, I'm out." Keep the frame in your template. Rewrite the opening lines for each guest, and cut anything that could fit any show.
Turn templates on

items: Choose Settings > See all settings in Gmail on your Mac.

blocks.text: Google's help page says you can only turn on and use message templates from Gmail on your computer. Do this setup at your Mac. You cannot use templates in the mobile app.
Save a pitch as a template

Write your pitch in a new message. Leave placeholders for the guest's name and the episode topic. Then go to More options > Templates > Save draft as template. Give the template a name that says who it is for, such as Founder interview or Coach interview.
Google's template page does not state a limit on how many templates you can save. A third-party guide claims a cap, but I could not confirm it, so do not plan around one.
Insert and delete Gmail templates without losing text

To insert a saved pitch, open a new message to the guest. Go to More options > Templates > Insert template and choose the pitch. The saved text drops in. Read the first line before you send. Check the guest's name, the show name and any date against the episode.

blocks.title: Read it aloud
blocks.text: Insert the template, then read the first line out loud. If it sounds like a form letter, rewrite it before you send.
Deleting is where people lose work. Google's help page is blunt: After you delete a template, you can't recover it. To delete one, go to More options > Templates > Delete template.

blocks.title: Back up before you delete
blocks.text: Copy the template text into Google Docs or Apple Notes before you delete anything. Google says a deleted template cannot be recovered.

Overwriting is safer when a pitch only needs an update. Open the draft, make the change, then use Save draft as template and choose the existing template to replace it. Read the name before you confirm, so you do not overwrite the pitch for a different kind of guest.
Schedule an email in Gmail on Mac across time zones

Scheduled send is the feature that makes time zones manageable. On a computer, click the arrow beside Send at the bottom left of the compose window. Choose a time. The message waits in the Scheduled folder until then.

Scheduled emails can still be edited. Open the Scheduled folder, then choose Cancel send. The message returns to a draft, so you can change it and schedule it again. Gmail allows up to 100 scheduled emails, according to Google's scheduling help.

Time zones need care. Google says scheduled emails go out based on the time zone you schedule them in. They can also leave a few minutes after the set time. Do not schedule a pitch for the exact minute a deadline closes.

Say you live in Chicago and your guest lives in London. You want the pitch to land in their morning, not in the middle of your night. Schedule it in the time zone you intend, then confirm the time in the Scheduled folder before you close the laptop.
Why generic podcast guest pitch emails fail

The numbers explain why careful pitches matter. In a Buzzsprout survey of 271 podcasters, the last three guests came mostly from the host's personal network. Cold email pitches supplied 28.0% of guests, the same share as referrals from past guests. The survey is self-reported, so treat it as a signal, not a law.

Cold pitches still have a door. Let's Make A Podcast looked at 383 readable feeds. It found 75% publish an email address as their contact route, and 12% publish no route at all. That study measures what feeds publish, not whether hosts reply, so it cannot tell you a reply rate.

Only 33% of shows showed visible evidence that they book guests. Adding recent episode notes raised that to 49%. A show that publishes guest notes gives you something specific to mention. Use that detail in the first line of your pitch.
Track guest booking email threads in Gmail

Booking can take weeks, so you need a system. Create a label for each stage, such as Pitched, Confirmed and Recorded. The steps are in [Create a label in Gmail](/how-to/create-a-label-in-gmail). Snooze a thread when you want it back on a certain day. The browser steps are in [Snooze an email in Gmail](/how-to/snooze-an-email-in-gmail).

Filters help when replies arrive in a steady stream. A filter can send mail from a host's domain to one label, so it stops crowding your inbox. The filter steps are in [Create a filter in Gmail](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail).

Some producers manage a host's inbox too. If the host wants you to handle their mail, they can grant delegate access. The steps are in [Give someone access to your mailbox in Gmail](/how-to/give-someone-access-to-your-mailbox-in-gmail). Agree with the host on what you may send before you start.
If you send a media kit or a release, the attachment steps and size limits are in [Attach a file in Gmail](/how-to/attach-a-file-in-gmail). Check the size before you send a large file.
Where Lazur fits in your Gmail work

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where the Send arrow is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Then you click it yourself.
Lazur does not click buttons for you. Ask how to save a template, and it guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on. You keep the mouse, and you choose what gets sent.
Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Gmail or any other app. It runs as its own app on your Mac, next to your browser. It drafts and types text, and it does not operate other apps for you.

Dictation is useful for follow-ups. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Add guest names and show names to the personal dictionary, so the spelling comes out right. Snippets and clipboard slots hold text you reuse.

Privacy matters when guest details are on screen. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps memory of what you asked and did, on the Mac.
A Pro trial is available with no credit card. It starts when you first open the app. Plans are on [the pricing page](/pricing), and you can get the app from the [download page](/download).
Research a guest before you pitch

A good pitch names something the guest actually said. Lazur can run research in its own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. When the job finishes, it returns a summary and a report. Your Gmail tab stays where it is while the research runs.

Ask for specifics. Name the guest, then ask for recent episodes, the topics they return to, and any claims they make about their work. Treat the summary as notes for your pitch, not as facts to quote. Check any claim against the episode itself.
Research example for one guest

Say your guest writes about hiring. Ask Lazur for a summary of their recent talks, then ask for the themes that repeat. Pick the theme that fits your show. Ask Lazur to draft a pitch that names that theme, then edit the draft by hand. Save the final version as a template for that kind of guest.
Mistakes to avoid in Gmail on a Mac

items: Setting up templates on your phone. Templates work only on a computer, so do the setup at your Mac.
Assuming the Chrome shortcut gives you macOS notifications. The guide says they are browser notifications.
Scheduling a pitch for the exact deadline. Scheduled sends can go out a few minutes late.
Deleting an old template to tidy up. Google says a deleted template cannot be recovered.
Sending one pitch to every show on a list. One guest survey respondent called an unsubscribe link a giveaway.
Expecting Lazur to press Send. It points, guides and drafts. You click.

faq.question: Is there a Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: A third-party Mac guide says there has never been an official Gmail app for Mac. Use Gmail in Safari or Chrome. A Chrome shortcut can give it its own Dock icon and window, but its alerts are browser notifications.

faq.question: Why don't my Gmail templates work on my phone?
faq.answer: Google says you can only turn on and use message templates from Gmail on your computer. Set them up at your Mac, then insert them from the compose window there.

faq.question: How many scheduled emails can I have in Gmail?
faq.answer: Google's scheduling help says you can have up to 100 scheduled emails. To change one, open the Scheduled folder and choose Cancel send. The message returns to a draft.

faq.question: Can I get back a template I deleted?
faq.answer: No. Google's template help says that after you delete a template, you can't recover it. Copy the text somewhere safe before you delete anything.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my emails for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It drafts and types text, points at controls and guides you one click at a time. You press Send.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my inbox?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Is Lazur a Gmail add-in?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app. It runs as its own app on your Mac, next to your browser, and it does not connect to Gmail as an add-in.
